raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan.

---

Our family has 13.1 mu. My husband and his older brother both do some work in town during the slow months, so it's mostly me managing the fields, with help at the busy times. With 4 people at home and only part-time labor, I can't handle too much cotton — picking is brutal. But we've always kept some cotton because the land on the west side is sandy and doesn't do as well for grain. So I split it: about 5 mu in cotton, and 8.1 mu in the wheat-maize rotation like most people in our village.

**Wheat** — I planted it last October, around the 10th, the window before the cold really set in. Used an improved variety I bought at the agro shop, nothing fancy, about 30 yuan per mu for seed. Before planting I spread compound fertilizer (15-15-15), about 40 kg per mu. Now in April the wheat is jointing and it looks alright — not too yellow, decent tiller count. I'll topdress urea soon, maybe 18 kg per mu, and irrigate at the same time because the ground is dry. Probably one more irrigation at filling if May is dry. The extension guy said you can get away with less N, but I'd rather put a little extra than watch my yield drop — one bad wheat year and we're buying flour. I'll hire the combine for harvest in early June, maybe 60 yuan per mu.

**Maize** — goes in right after wheat harvest, mid-June. No time to plow, nobody does around here anymore — we use the no-till direct seeder, I pay the village guy about 25 yuan per mu to run his machine. Hybrid seed, same brand as last year because my neighbor and I both got over 450 kg/mu with it. Compound fertilizer at planting, urea topdress when it's knee-high. One irrigation at tasseling if it hasn't rained. Maize is easier than wheat honestly — less water, less fuss.

**Cotton** — planting now. I buy Bt hybrid seed, expensive at 80 yuan per mu but without it the bollworms eat everything. I plow and harrow the cotton fields before planting because the sandy soil needs it. Base fertilizer of compound, then urea at squaring and again when bolls are setting — three times total. Two irrigations usually. Herbicide before planting, and I spray for aphids and whiteflies when I see them — can't be strict about it, I just watch the leaves. Picking starts in September and I do it myself over 6-7 weeks. It's the hardest part of the year.

Budget this year is tight — grain prices aren't great and fertilizer is still expensive. I'm not trying anything new. What worked last year will work this year.
